source.title: Demystify Optimization and Generalization of Over-parameterized PAC-Bayesian Learning
source.authors: Wei Huang; Chunrui Liu; Yilan Chen; Tian-Yu Liu; R. Xu

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices and references, is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports empirical results about how width affects parameter movement during training and training-free proxy correlations with generalization bounds. These are related to generalization but do not test the catalog versions’ natural-label train/test error claims or named measures of the generalization gap.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported experiments measuring parameter changes during training and correlations between the proposed proxy PA and generalization bounds. The reported testing-error values in Table 1 are outcomes of the paper's hyperparameter search and are not a test of any listed claim version, so they are not rows. Theoretical bounds and cited results are not empirical rows.
record.test_reason: Table 1 bears on V3: convolutional networks have lower held-out error than fully connected networks on both MNIST and CIFAR-10 under both hyperparameter-selection methods. These are probabilistic networks trained with PAC-Bayesian objectives and data-dependent priors, extending the architectural comparison to a different training setting. Weight-movement and proxy-to-bound correlations do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors characterize wide probabilistic-network training through PNTK, obtain a kernel ridge regression solution under their assumptions, derive a PAC-Bayesian bound they argue improves over a corresponding Rademacher bound, and demonstrate efficient hyperparameter selection with PA.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and trains probabilistic neural networks using PAC-Bayesian bound objectives, rather than the natural-label classification and interventions in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported proxy-to-bound correlations vary with dataset, architecture, and selected hyperparameter: on CIFAR10 CNN the reported ρ0 correlation is 0.57, versus 0.83 for KL penalty and 0.89 for prior-data proportion.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative parameter movement decreases with width: input/output layers scale as 1/√m and hidden layers as 1/m.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide probabilistic networks trained with the tested PAC-Bayesian objective move less relative to initialization as width increases.

fits_no_version.finding: PA correlates with computed PAC-Bayesian bounds across selected hyperparameters, with reported Kendall correlations from 0.57 to 0.93 and an aggregated correlation of 0.7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training-free PA proxy can rank computed PAC-Bayesian bounds in the tested hyperparameter searches.

record.problems: The experiments use limited settings: one fixed MNIST subset for weight movement and selected MNIST/CIFAR10 architectures for proxy correlations. The paper reports no direct comparison of natural-label training and test errors or of train/test gaps for the catalog versions. Correlation significance is stated for the MNIST results; no uncertainty is given for the CIFAR10 correlations.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports testing error and generalization-bound values for hyperparameter selections by Brute-Force and PA on MNIST/CIFAR10 with FCN/CNN. These are search outcomes for the proposed proxy method, not results testing any listed version, so they are not rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold; parameter-movement scaling cannot establish this.
The causal contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, convolutional initialization of fully connected networks, and comparisons on CIFAR-100 or SVHN.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus measured generalization gaps and competing measures.
Retraining after removing memorized versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: Add MNIST architectural test-error comparisons: CNN 0.0091 versus FCN 0.0192 under brute-force selection; CNN 0.0168 versus FCN 0.0213 under PA. Both show the V3 effect as observed.
Add CIFAR-10 architectural test-error comparisons: CNN 0.1514 versus FCN 0.4840 under brute-force selection; CNN 0.1510 versus FCN 0.4905 under PA. Both show the V3 effect as observed.

record.verdict_notes: The record declares Table 1 omitted, but its reason for exclusion is too broad: comparisons between PA and brute-force selection concern the proposed method, while CNN-versus-FCN held-out errors within each selector bear on V3. These architecture comparisons use separately selected hyperparameters and do not isolate local connectivity as the cause.

versions.untested_parts: Whether models that fit random labels generalize on natural labels, and random-label held-out accuracy.
Whether widening beyond the interpolation threshold lowers test error on natural labels.
Comparative convolutional versus fully connected test error and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning and decay recipes.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Effects of dropout and weight decay on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train/test gaps against other measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.
